submitted.content: Fair bounded run under systemd-run: ACT dump_from_zipper writes state.act plus fixed-width state.values sidecar; ACT warm exact lookup reads trie ordinal and slices equivalent 128-byte payload; LMDB uses production LmdbKeyValueStore batch put/get. Sizes 256, 4096, 16384; Criterion sample-size 10, warm-up 1s, measurement 1s. ACT write throughput: 2.8688, 7.0871, 7.0190 Melem/s. LMDB write: 1.1001, 1.9473, 1.9729. ACT lookup: 2.0660, 1.7150, 1.4563. LMDB lookup: 3.0735, 2.8560, 2.5571. ACT bytes: 33386, 540825, 2164585. LMDB bytes: 86016, 884736, 3436544. Interpretation: ACT writes faster and is more compact in this fixture; LMDB batch lookup is faster. Not a production backend verdict: incremental WAL, crash recovery, concurrent writers, and all RSpace namespaces remain unmeasured. See Appendix J and commits 53b5ef356, 0c1d01ceb, 87a9584b3.
submitted.label: ACT versus LMDB fair bounded matrix

submitted.content: Bounded systemd-run cargo test -p rspace_plus_plus --test rho_path_spec --no-fail-fast passed 20/20 in 0.14s. Covered V2 framing, malformed rejection, prefix queries, nested value skipping, and million-byte fields on a small native stack. This is codec verification only; it does not establish lifecycle activation or production persistence migration.
submitted.label: RhoPathV2 bounded codec verification

submitted.content: Bounded systemd-run cargo test -p rspace_plus_plus --test mod continuation_join_lifecycle --no-fail-fast passed 1/1: continuation_join_lifecycle_equivalence::legacy_and_pathmap_continuation_join_lifecycles_are_identical. The fixture compares PathMap-backed hot-store lifecycle with the legacy oracle across continuation/join setup, duplicate/order behavior, checkpoint/reset, export/import, replay, and post-state fields. This is one focused differential, not full V1/V2 production activation.
submitted.label: RhoPathV2 lifecycle differential

submitted.content: Bounded systemd-run cargo test -p rspace_plus_plus --lib retention --no-fail-fast passed 15/15 in 0.06s. Covers generation lease blocking/release, transactional unknown/overflow release, deterministic retained-root snapshots, manifest validation, rewrite differential, and durable publication retention requirements.

reproducibility_checklist: Pin each arm to a single CCD with `taskset -c <cores>` (or sched_setaffinity) to remove cross-CCD L3/NUMA variance.
Set every pinned core to the `performance` governor (`cpupower frequency-set -g performance`); record scaling_driver + boost state.
Record the full hardware string (first H1 of ~/.claude/hardware-specifications.md), `uname -a`, and the CPU model in host_meta.
Record the exact commands / tool invocations, the git SHA of each arm, and a fixed RNG seed.
Tee benchmark output to a file and run once — do not re-run to cherry-pick a favorable result.
Discard warm-up replicates; measure only after the series reaches steady state.
